title: Server functions: size, cold start, per-request overhead
headline: One import cycle of 229 server modules makes 559 of 562 pages, 181 of 268 route handlers and the proxy load the same 11 MB of server code: re-measured in this pass, such an entry needs 0.84 to 1.09 s and 71 to 83 MB to start where a route outside the cycle needs 0.16 s and 14 MB, and a start hook adds 0.33 s before any request. None of this rests on a feature being unused; every store pays it after each deploy (90 commits to main on 11 November), on scale-out and after idle, and it grows at opening as many quiet stores meet cold instances. Thirteen findings stand (eleven verified, two added) and seven of them are import changes with no data moved: on the import graph they take the visit beacon from 1,306 source files to about 100, the proxy from 1,309 to about 95 and a storefront page from about 1,420 to about 600, where the page renderer is the floor. Added by this pass: every store's own domain is compiled into each deployment (4 to 8 routing rules a store against Vercel's 2,048 a deployment, of which this app's own dynamic routes already take 685, and a full redeploy per domain change), and the list of those domains is parsed again for every link a page draws.

clean: Nothing in this dimension argues from 'no store uses it'. Every finding is a cost paid per cold start, per request, per build or per store, whatever a store uses. The two that lean on production's counts (the start hook's query, the nine every-minute routes) are read as idle cost, and FN-10 is ranked last for that reason.

The routes outside the cycle show the floor and are well made: /api/health loads 17 chunks (1.14 MB) and starts in 159 to 163 ms with 14.4 MB; /api/ab/assign 1.56 MB, 240 ms, 22.2 MB; /api/consent and /api/csp-report reach 55 and 54 source files.

A server-side await import() does give a chunk that loads on demand in this build: the files six light handlers import only lazily are absent from their start chunks, and the start hook's own entry file is 169 bytes: its 2.33 MB of chunks load only when register() runs. 58 such imports already exist in 30 files of src/server. The rule about import() in docs/performance.md:39 is about a visitor's client scripts, not server chunks.

Chromium is traced only into the routes that launch it (three cron routes, the replicator's tick, two admin PDF routes, the shopper's document PDF, the PDF job); Playwright, @sparticuz/chromium, unpdf and mammoth are imported on demand (src/server/browser.ts:11-15). playwright-core's JS is also traced into four replicator entries that start no browser: small.

The proxy's per-request work is light when warm: no fetch, pure decisions in src/lib, one store-facts read per store per instance per 10 s (src/server/redirect-resolve.ts:203-232), A/B tests read only with the kaizen_ab cookie, held-domain lookups only for hosts that are no store's, the 404 count after the response. The 10-second bound serves private mode, so it is not a finding. The one per-request cost that grows is the hosts list (FN-12).
No client component imports a server-only module, directly or through src/lib: 0 of 495 client files on the graph; 787 modules carry import "server-only".

Environment variables are validated when used, not at import. The database pool is created on the first db() call, 5 connections, 5 s idle (src/db/client.ts:14, 63-71, 95-98). Keeping an instance running until its idle connections close (attachDatabasePool, line 77) is by design and is weighed in the scheduled-work plan (CR-1), not here.

No route sets a runtime; nothing is on the edge runtime, which fits cacheComponents. All 13 cron routes have a maxDuration; eleven run through trackedRoute(), the five-minute dispatcher runs its jobs through runJobs(), and /api/cron/document-pdfs is left out on purpose (src/server/cron-routes.scan.test.ts). The shopper chat route sets no maxDuration; what bounds it is the project's default, which was not visible, and its AI calls time out at 30 s by themselves.
Next loads a handler's own code lazily (userland behind a require), and source maps (about 672 MB of the build) are in no function trace.

JSON imported as modules is small (google-fonts.json 71 KB, no-saft.json 88 KB). The 13 MB taxonomy is read from disk on first use, not at import, and the product page reads it inside a cached function.

src/lib/page-content.ts (4,319 lines) costs little at import: it is not among the costliest files of the cold-load profile. The zod cost at start comes mostly from the AI manager's tool definitions (src/lib/owner-tools.ts, about 44 ms in the profile), which FN-1 takes out of every entry but the AI's own.
The docs' Markdown (0.8 MB) and HarfBuzz's wasm (0.7 MB) are traced only into the 22 and 1 entries that read them.

One import-graph test already exists and is sound: src/lib/pay-routes.graph.test.ts keeps forbidden modules off the pay routes and follows import() too, so the lazy imports planned here cannot hide a module from it.
The list of every store's hosts does not reach the browser (the verified client-bundles report: no client chunk parses NEXT_PUBLIC_STORE_HOSTS).

findings.title: One import cycle makes nearly every function load the whole application
findings.evidence: Re-measured in this pass. Source, from my own graph (TypeScript parser, 4,136 non-test files of src, type-only imports dropped): 229 files of src/server form one cycle (96,162 lines); importing any one of them reaches 1,305 files, 384,586 lines. 179 of 265 route.ts handlers, 436 of 560 pages by their own imports, 18 of 24 layouts and the proxy reach it. Build: 559 of 562 pages list the same 11.50 MB (145 chunks) of server JS for loading at start, and 181 of 268 handlers the same 10.85 MB (113 chunks). Cold load in a fresh process, 2 runs each: /api/health 159 to 163 ms and 14.4 MB of heap; /robots.txt 907 to 932 ms and 77.6 MB; /api/visit 933 to 945 ms and 77.6 MB with sharp's native binary loaded; the storefront home 1,007 to 1,085 ms and 83.1 MB; the admin's Orders page 1,015 to 1,055 ms and 82.1 MB. Twenty-four public handlers of 7 to 52 lines of their own (robots.txt, the sitemaps, llms.txt, favicon.ico, the admin's manifest, the blog feeds, unsubscribe, the beacons, shop tiles) each reach 1,306 to 1,309 files. I opened all six named imports: each is used at one or two call sites inside async functions. Cutting them takes the largest cycle 229, 88, 57, 29, 19; cycles of 19, 11, 8 and 3 files remain. A lazy import does stay out of the start chunks in this build: six handlers outside the cycle reach 15 files only through await import(), and none of the 15 is in the chunks those handlers load at start (read from the chunks' source maps). A side effect: 74 cached functions of modules in the cycle (seo.ts 6, custom-fields.ts 6, experiments.ts 5 and others) are each listed for 500 to 804 entries in the 10.4 MB server-action manifest (1,454 ids, 55.7 entries each on average, median 2).
findings.cost: About 0.75 to 0.9 s and 63 to 69 MB of heap per cold instance above the 0.16 s and 14 MB floor, on about 740 of 830 entries. Also a 50 MB median trace and a 10.4 MB action manifest.
findings.who_pays: The first shopper or owner on each new instance: after every deploy (90 commits to main on 11 November), on scale-out, after idle. The server pays the memory per instance; the build pays the size. It grows at opening: many stores with little traffic each mean a larger share of requests meets a cold instance.

findings.title: The proxy runs before every page and prefetch, and loads the whole application to do six small reads
findings.evidence: The proxy is a Node function (Next 16's default) and its matcher takes every page address with its prefetches: one page view sends 13 to 54 requests through it (verified report, from the local production build; not re-run). Re-measured here: its trace is 343 files and 45.7 MB (sharp and libvips 18.9, taxonomy 12.7, chunks 12.5); a cold load takes 838 to 884 ms (2 runs) with 70.9 MB of heap, 151 MB RSS and sharp's native binary loaded. On my graph it reaches 1,309 source files. I traced each of its six server imports: house-switch.ts (pagesTag from ./pages, STORES_TAG from ./seo, audit from ./auth) and redirect-resolve.ts (catalogTag from ./catalog at line 19) reach the cycle; holding.ts and not-found.ts reach 315 and 332 files because the proxy's read sits beside admin writers that import ./auth and ./permissions; redirect-resolve.ts also takes countHit from ./redirects (329 files) and recordNotFound from ./not-found; experiments.ts reaches 108 files (the page model and media-alts). Simulated with those edges cut and the reads in leaves: 136 files with experiments.ts as it is, 89 with its two reads in a leaf too, none of them auth.ts, admin-text.ts or the Stripe SDK. One scan test already holds the proxy's direct imports by name (redirect-writers.test.ts:122-131), but nothing holds what those modules import in turn.
findings.cost: About 0.65 s and 50 MB more than a lean route on every cold proxy instance, in front of every page of every store, cached pages included.
findings.who_pays: Every shopper and visitor whose request meets a new proxy instance; the server's memory. The cron routes do not keep it warm (the matcher leaves /api out), so quiet hours and each deploy leave it cold.

findings.done_when: In CI's hosts job a domain activated after the build serves its store's front page, and .next/routes-manifest.json holds the same number of redirects and rewrites whether the database has 0 or 300 active store domains.
findings.saving: Estimate: one production deployment fewer per domain change (each a full build that empties the caches and restarts every function cold), 4 to 8 routing rules fewer per store with a domain, and no ceiling near 270 such stores. No per-request gain: a remembered read replaces a rule match.
findings.risk: This is every store's front door on its own domain: a mistake takes those stores off the air, where today a mistake is caught at build. A lookup must fail open to the answer the platform gives today for an unknown host, never to another store. The 60 s memory means a removed domain answers for up to a minute. The proxy would run on more requests (a store's files with an extension on own domains). It would be noticed by CI's hosts job and e2e/store-hosts.spec.ts; step 2 comes first because the ceiling may be nearer or further than estimated.
